function: PPO actor outputs UAV flight speed and angle, sub-carrier assignment scores (reconstructed to discrete) and vehicle transmit power; vehicle-UAV association comes from improved k-means (p. 6-7, 9).
system: UAV-assisted vehicular uplink: 2 rotary-wing UAVs as aerial BSs, 7 vehicles, OFDMA with 5 shared 1 MHz sub-carriers, 2 GHz; antennas not stated (p. 3-4, 11).
method: PPO-clip actor-critic RL (on-policy) with improved k-means for association and action reconstruction for sub-carriers; 28,000 episodes, hidden width 150, learning rate 0.001 (p. 8-11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: probabilistic LoS/NLoS path loss with elevation-dependent LoS probability; 1000 x 1000 m2 area, random roads, vehicle speed 24-72 km/h; no dataset (p. 4, 11).
test_conditions: Trained on random vehicle trajectories, tested on random trajectories; convergence per network size (2-3 UAVs, 5-11 vehicles); sweeps of speed, speed error, altitude, QoS, power (p. 12-15).
baselines: Learned: IKDDPG (improved k-means with DDPG), PPO with direct association. Fixed or ablated: random trajectory, static UAVs, and no power control, no association, no sub-carrier optimization (p. 11).
metrics: System total reward, system energy efficiency (sum rate over UAV flight power), convergence episodes, per-slot execution time (p. 11-15).
complexity: Big-O O(2EN sum N_i(in) N_(i+1)(out)); measured per-slot execution time below 0.005 s, mean 0.0017-0.0035 s (Table IV) (p. 11-12).
q1_support: p. 4: "We employ the probabilistic path loss model to describe the" - custom LoS/NLoS model with elevation-dependent LoS probability (eqs. 7-12); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 12: "optimization, we conduct tests using a variety of randomly" - tests use random trajectories of the same generator; Fig. 10 shows convergence per network size, and the paper never says a trained model is reused in a new scenario.
q3_support: p. 11: "f) IKDDPG, the joint optimization scheme by combining the"; p. 11: "which applies random UAV trajectory"; p. 14: "the system EE achieved by the proposed IKPP, consistently"
q4_support: p. 11: "the overall complexity" of IKPP is O(2EN sum N_i(in) N_(i+1)(out)); p. 12: "time slot is below 0.005 s, with many of them as low as around"
q5_support: p. 11: "The simulations are conducted using Python 3.8 and" - self-generated simulation; no code or data link and no public dataset.
notes: Included under rule 4: PPO outputs sub-carrier assignment, vehicle transmit power and UAV trajectory (p. 6-7, 9), and in an aerial link learned power and resource control is physical layer (area 6); vehicle association comes from the non-learned improved k-means (p. 7). Borderline q2: Table V (speed error, p. 13) and Fig. 12 (vehicle speed 3-18 m/s, partly below the training interval of 24-72 km/h, p. 11) may be tests under new conditions, but the paper does not say the trained model is reused without retraining, so q2 is 0; reviewer to confirm. q3 counts IKDDPG (DDPG architecture of [20] with the same k-means) as the learned baseline and random-trajectory and static-UAV schemes as non-learned baselines; the PPO scheme and the NOP, NOA, NOB variants are ablations and are not counted.
